title: $(2,q)$-hypercontractivity for even exponents
statement:
Let $q \ge 2$ be an even integer, and let $\rho \in \bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2 \le \tfrac{1}{q-1}$. Then for every Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ contracts from $L^2$ to $L^q$ in the sense that
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^q\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{q/2},
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: q is an integer with q ≥ 2
f is a Boolean function on {0,1}^n
replaced:
For an even integer $q \ge 2$ and noise parameter $\rho$ with $\rho^2 \le 1/(q-1)$,
\[
  \E[(T_\rho f)^q] \le \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{q/2}.
\]
This is the $(2,2k)$ theorem restated in terms of an even exponent $q = 2k$.
